name: Alice's Pudding
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: ½ cup strawberry or other sweet jam
ingredients.originalText: ½ cup strawberry or other sweet jam

instructions.text: Pour over these half a cup jam, and cover this well with the rest of the crumbs, wet with a very little milk
Heat the quart of milk until near boiling, take it from the fire and add, gradually, the beaten yolks and sugar, stirring in the beaten whites lightly at the last
Heat this by degrees, stirring constantly until it begins to thicken
Put it, spoonful by spoonful, upon the layer of bread-crumbs, taking care not to disturb these
Bake until well "set" and very slightly browned

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Butter a pudding-dish
2. Sprinkle the bottom with bread-crumbs
3. Pour over these half a cup jam, and cover this well with the rest of the crumbs, wet with a very little milk
4. Heat the quart of milk until near boiling, take it from the fire and add, gradually, the beaten yolks and sugar, stirring in the beaten whites lightly at the last
5. Heat this by degrees, stirring constantly until it begins to thicken
6. Put it, spoonful by spoonful, upon the layer of bread-crumbs, taking care not to disturb these
7. Bake until well "set" and very slightly browned
8. Eat cold
originalIngredients: ½ cup strawberry or other sweet jam
